behaviors.title: Reference conversion is deterministic and bounded
invariants: Identical source pixels and validated options yield identical result pixels.
Transparent areas remain transparent and configured palette ceilings remain bounded.
Applying a mask changes only output alpha and never rewrites source RGB channels.
Locked palettes bound every processed material region to the selected asset family colors.
Every artifact and manifest identifies the result as a reference underpainting.

scenarios.title: Malformed recipes never reach image processing
scenarios.oracle: Out-of-range widths, palette counts, dithering, edge thresholds, cluster sizes, invalid region IDs, and malformed polygons are rejected at worker and CLI boundaries.

scenarios.title: Browser recipes replay through the CLI
scenarios.oracle: A browser-exported project recipe can be parsed by the CLI and creates the documented artifact bundle with source hash, metrics, and palettes.

scenarios.title: Cutout operations preserve the subject and remain local
scenarios.oracle: Connected-background clearing is bounded by color tolerance, hard brush edits affect only mask alpha, imported masks resample deterministically, and transparent trimming preserves requested padding.

scenarios.title: Canonical sprite exports use exact integer scaling
scenarios.oracle: The resize command emits a 1x canonical PNG, requested 2x through 16x nearest-neighbor PNGs with exact integer dimensions, and a replayable asset manifest.

behaviors.title: The browser workbench processes images locally
invariants: The application has no source-image upload endpoint or remote processing dependency.
Cutout tools, material regions, diagnostics, palette counts, and exports remain keyboard reachable.
The browser exports one canonical sprite and exact integer display scales rather than inventing responsive detail.
The UI never presents an automated result as finished pixel art.

scenarios.title: A local image produces visible output and diagnostics
scenarios.oracle: After file selection, the workbench reports Ready, renders the underpainting and diagnostics, exposes exports, and displays the human-cleanup provenance warning.

scenarios.title: A local background cutout is visible and reversible
scenarios.oracle: After selecting a connected background, the workbench renders the transparent cutout, exposes bounded undo and redo, and keeps canonical scale exports available without any network request.

behaviors.title: Aseprite handoff is explicit and non-destructive
invariants: Aseprite is invoked only when --aseprite is present.
The handoff writes only inside the selected output directory and does not alter Aseprite preferences or install extensions.
The underpainting layer is visible and diagnostic layers are hidden.

scenarios.title: A missing Aseprite binary fails with an exact repair path
scenarios.oracle: The CLI keeps the PNG/JSON bundle and reports that ASEPRITE_BIN or --aseprite-bin is required without claiming the .aseprite artifact exists.
